hotspots.label: logo
hotspots.title: Mazda Logo
hotspots.description: , introduced in 1997 and refined over time, is inspired by the letter "M" stylized as a pair of outstretched wings inside an oval. Designed by Rei Yoshimara, the elegant V-shaped wings symbolize continuous growth, flexible thinking, creativity, and the freedom to soar into the future.

hotspots.label: wheel
hotspots.title: Standard 19 inch wheel
hotspots.description: Mazda 3: Factory rim sizes range from 16x6.5 inches on base trims up to 18x7 inches on higher or turbo trims. Most modern generations use a standard 5x114.3mm bolt pattern and a 67.1mm center bore.

hotspots.label: headlight
hotspots.title: Cheetah's Eye Headlight
hotspots.description: When Mazda introduced the first generation of its Kodo design language, designers explicitly drew inspiration from the focused, intense eyes of a cheetah stalked and ready to pounce on its prey. This inspired the inner circular LED rings surrounded by sharp, predatory outer lens housing.

hotspots.label: sideMirror
hotspots.title: Side Mirror
hotspots.description: Mazda crafts its side mirror housings using the "Kodo: Soul of Motion" design language, mirroring organic, fluid lines found in nature to reduce wind noise and drag.

hotspots.label: steeringWheel
hotspots.title: Steering Wheel
hotspots.description: Mazda applies the Japanese principle of miyabei (elegance by removing the unnecessary) and shibui (subtle, unobtrusive beauty) to cockpit ergonomics.

hotspots.label: ac
hotspots.title: AC Vent
hotspots.description: Jet-Engine Aesthetic: The round eyeball architecture mimics vintage aircraft afterburners or turbine cowlings, evoking a sense of speed and mechanical engagement.

hotspots.label: skyactiv
hotspots.title: Mazda Skyactiv Technology
hotspots.description: a holistic engineering philosophy introduced in 2011 to optimize a vehicle's entire ecosystem—including the engine, transmission, body, and chassis—to maximize performance and fuel efficiency without relying solely on electrification.
